title: SDK compatibility and streaming + pagination requirements across Python/TS/Go
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD snapshot: We need a cross-language SDK contract for Python, TypeScript, and Go that standardizes pagination, retry behavior, streaming APIs, and compatibility guarantees for the Redwood Inference public SDKs. Goal: deliver consistent developer ergonomics and stable semantics across SDKs so product teams can migrate between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments without subtle behavioral differences. This ticket defines requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for the next minor SDK release. Scope: -- Required: 1) Pagination helpers with cursor semantics and an idiomatic default (auto-pagination helpers + manual cursor access) for list endpoints. 2) Retry policy with configurable strategy (exponential backoff + jitter), idempotency detection, and clear defaults for requests that mutate versus read-only. 3) Streaming APIs supporting: server-sent events (SSE) fallback for browsers/TS, HTTP2/gRPC for high-throughput private deployments, and chunked-transfer/async iterator patterns in Python and Go. 4) Backwards compatibility policy: surface stability matrix, deprecation window (>= 3 months), and migration guidance. 5) Tests and CI jobs: cross-language contract tests validating pagination ordering, resume from cursor, retry idempotency, and streaming reconnect semantics. -- Out of scope: language-specific feature additions (e.g., TS-only utility types), deep client-side state machines for every streaming transport. Assumptions: API servers expose a stable cursor token for list endpoints and return consistent ordering with pagination token semantics. Streaming endpoints provide event markers for message boundaries and include server-side sequence numbers. Decision summary: - Use cursor-based pagination (opaque token) rather than page-number offsets to support large result sets and ensure consistent ordering across deployments. - Default page size: 100 items; max page size: 1000. SDKs must expose page_size parameter and validate against max. - Auto-pagination helpers: Python -> async iterator (.stream_items()), TS -> async iterable (for await ... of), Go -> iterator struct with Next() bool / Value() pattern. - Retry default: idempotent requests (GET/list/embeddings) use retry with exponential backoff starting at 100ms, max 5 retries, jitter-enabled. Non-idempotent requests default to no retries but support opt-in with explicit idempotency token. - Streaming: provide a unified high-level streaming abstraction called "StreamReader" in all SDKs that yields message objects and supports cancellation, checkpointing, and reconnection policy. Trade-offs: - Cursor-based pagination increases server-side state dependencies but provides strong resume semantics. - Unified streaming abstraction hides transport differences; advanced users can still access raw transport layer when needed. Migration impact: - Existing customers using offset-based clients must follow migration guide which includes sample scripts and compatibility shim for 6 months. - Breaking changes are only allowed under major version; this release is minor and must not introduce breaking surface changes to method names or parameter types.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Pagination - SDKs include both auto-pagination helpers and manual cursor APIs. Auto-pagination must iterate in stable order and allow an optional max_items cap.
AC2: Cursor resume - Given a cursor token returned from page N, all SDKs can resume from that cursor and return the same remaining items in the same order.
AC3: Retry behavior - Default retry policy applied to idempotent endpoints across SDKs; configuration surface documented and overrideable per-request and per-client.
AC4: Idempotency tokens - SDKs expose a standard header/parameter helper for attaching idempotency tokens; server will honor and deduplicate by token.

AC5: Streaming - High-level StreamReader abstraction implemented in Python/TS/Go; supports cancellation, per-event sequence numbers, and reconnection with resume where the server supports checkpoint tokens.

AC6: Transport fallbacks - TS SDK streams via SSE in browsers and via native WebSocket/HTTP2 in Node; Python stream uses HTTP chunked with async iterator; Go provides HTTP2/gRPC streaming implementation. Each SDK must expose raw transport hooks for advanced users.
AC7: Compatibility policy - No public method renames or param type changes in this minor release; deprecated signatures must be present with deprecation warnings for at least 3 months.
AC8: Tests - Cross-language contract test suite added to CI verifying pagination ordering, retry attempts, and streaming reconnection/resume behavior.
AC9: Docs - Migration guide, samples for Python/TS/Go, and CHANGELOG entry published before release.
AC10: Telemetry - SDKs emit consistent telemetry events for pagination fetch, retry attempt, stream reconnect, and fatal streaming error. Events documented in observability spec.
qa_steps: Step 1: Run contract tests in CI across Python/TS/Go to verify identical item sequences from sample list endpoint using generated dataset.
Step 2: Simulate transient network error and confirm retry policy triggers expected backoff and stops after configured attempts for idempotent calls.
Step 3: Start a streaming session, ingest 500 small events, kill connection at event #237, then reconnect and use checkpoint token to resume. Verify no duplicates and ordering preserved.
Step 4: Validate auto-pagination helpers stop at max_items and surface errors when server returns malformed cursor token.
Step 5: Lint and type-check TS SDK (strict mode) and run Python static analysis (mypy), run go vet and integration tests.
Step 6: Verify telemetry events are emitted and appear in console staging dashboard for pagination/retry/stream events.
Step 7: Manual docs review by DX and a sample-app integration verifying migration steps for offset->cursor migration.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Cursor token incompatibilities between older servers and new SDK behavior. Mitigation: add compatibility shim in SDKs to detect offset-style tokens and translate or throw clear error with migration hint.
Risk: Streaming recovery not supported by some private deployments. Mitigation: StreamReader will expose "use_checkpoint" flag with graceful fallback to resume=false and clear developer warning.
Risk: Retry policy causing duplicate side-effects. Mitigation: default to no retries for non-idempotent endpoints and provide idempotency-token utilities in SDKs.
Risk: Increased surface area for breaking changes. Mitigation: enforce strict acceptance criteria and automated contract tests for release gating.
